title: Strontium fluoride: Ksp and a common ion

stimulus.title: A slightly soluble fluoride
stimulus.html: Strontium fluoride, SrF2, is slightly soluble in water: SrF2(s) ⇌ Sr2+(aq) + 2 F−(aq). At 25 °C, Ksp = 4.3 × 10−9. NaF is a soluble salt.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the expression for Ksp of SrF2.

rubric.point: K<sub>sp</sub> = [Sr²⁺][F⁻]², with the solid left out.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the molar solubility of SrF2 in pure water at 25 °C.

accept: setup with 4s³; [F⁻] must be 2s and squared

parts.sample: [Sr<sup>2+</sup>] = s and [F<sup>−</sup>] = 2s. K<sub>sp</sub> = s(2s)<sup>2</sup> = 4s<sup>3</sup> = 4.3 × 10<sup>−9</sup>, so s<sup>3</sup> = 1.08 × 10<sup>−9</sup> and s = 1.0 × 10<sup>−3</sup> M.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate the molar solubility of SrF2 in 0.10 M NaF at 25 °C.
parts.sample: [F<sup>−</sup>] = 0.10 + 2s ≈ 0.10 M. K<sub>sp</sub> = s(0.10)<sup>2</sup>, so s = 4.3 × 10<sup>−9</sup> / 0.010 = 4.3 × 10<sup>−7</sup> M. (2s is negligible next to 0.10 M.)

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A student claims that NaF lowers the solubility of SrF2 because it lowers the value of Ksp. Explain what is wrong with the claim, using Q and Ksp.

rubric.point: K<sub>sp</sub> is unchanged (it depends only on temperature); added F⁻ raises Q = [Sr²⁺][F⁻]² above K<sub>sp</sub>, so SrF₂ precipitates (or less dissolves) until Q = K<sub>sp</sub>.
accept: the common ion increases Q, not decreases K

parts.sample: K<sub>sp</sub> does not change; it depends only on temperature. The F<sup>−</sup> from NaF increases Q = [Sr<sup>2+</sup>][F<sup>−</sup>]<sup>2</sup>, so Q exceeds K<sub>sp</sub> at a lower [Sr<sup>2+</sup>]. Less SrF<sub>2</sub> dissolves before Q = K<sub>sp</sub>, so the solubility is lower.
